questions.question: Which two categories across all three pie charts share exactly the same percentage value, and what is that value?
questions.expected_answer: Limiter and Negation in the Categorical chart, both at 27.91%

questions.question: What is the ratio of the largest slice in the Approximate Number Generation chart to the smallest slice in the Categorical chart? Round to one decimal place.
If you sum the two smallest slices from the Categorical chart and compare that sum to the largest slice in the Approximate Number Generation chart, which is larger and by how much?
questions.expected_answer: The sum of Existential Quantifiers (15.12%) and Limiter (27.91%) is 43.03%, which is less than Approximate Quantities (45.03%) by 2.00 percentage points

questions.question: How many individual slices across all three pie charts have a percentage value below 20%?
questions.expected_answer: 2 (Existential Quantifiers at 15.12% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%)

questions.question: What is the difference in percentage points between the most evenly split chart and the least evenly split chart, measured as the range (max slice minus min slice) within each chart?
questions.expected_answer: Disjunctive & Conjunctive range: 50.49 - 49.51 = 0.98; Categorical range: 29.07 - 15.12 = 13.95; Approximate Number Generation range: 45.03 - 18.71 = 26.32. Difference between least even and most even: 26.32 - 0.98 = 25.34 percentage points

questions.expected_answer: MEND (~49%) and MEMIT (~51%) are closest, approximately 2 percentage points apart

questions.question: Which SepLLM variant converges to the lowest final loss, and approximately what is its final loss value?
